far.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer, production game scene layer edit. Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: retain its exact scene content, canvas alignment and silhouette, but REPAINT ALL VISIBLE SURFACES in the project's default painting technique. Images 2-3 are STYLE REFERENCES ONLY: observe the opaque, overlapping angular brush planes on the gray hair and dark dress, with large coherent shadow groups and locally denser structural strokes. Images 4-5 are STYLE REFERENCES ONLY for subtle chromatic gray overpainting, varied hand-drawn edges, selective line weight, broad calm fields and deliberate strokes. Do NOT copy ANY people, faces, costume, ribbons, reference palette, white backdrop, handwriting, signatures or watermark. Apply that technique to snow, metal, glass and architecture. This must read as a substantial artist-painted material pass, not a barely visible retouch or filter. Hand-painted Japanese anime environment, opaque gouache-like color blocks, firm light-shadow shapes, visible purposeful broad and short brush edges, slight warm/cool value shifts that follow volume. Quiet large planes alternate with a few resolved structural accents. Matte steel is dark chromatic blue-gray with selected narrow dull highlights; snow is chalky warm-white and lavender/blue-gray sculpted planes, not fluffy plastic icing. Preserve existing cold winter atmosphere and restrained small warm lamp-light accents, keep darks readable. NO airbrush gloss, glossy 3D, flat vector fills, uniformly thick black outlines, photo grain, evenly distributed noise, mushy watercolor texture, random triangular confetti, new objects, people, game UI, words or logos. Output EXACT full canvas 1659x948 with composition and object locations unchanged.
LAYER: fully opaque distant winter backdrop only. Preserve exact horizon, broad cloud shapes, elevated bridge running horizontally around y440 with the same three pier locations, distant low city silhouettes around y540 and open misty snowfield. Do not add snow foreground, canopy, lamps, shelter or figures. Repaint broad cloud masses into coherent restrained cool blue-gray/lavender planes using directional opaque strokes and selective broken edges; let large quiet sky shapes remain, not an evenly mottled sponge texture. Bridge is simple broad matte gray structural planes, distant silhouettes low contrast and unfussy. Mist and reflected snow light should have atmospheric depth but be built from layered broad paint bands, not airbrushed smooth gradients or blanket blur. Keep the original relative value hierarchy so figures remain focal over this backdrop. Maintain a unified cold dusk blue-gray base with subtle lilac and pale warm gray in lighter planes, not a new sunset. EXACT 1659x948 landscape composition, full opaque background, no alpha needed.
